2. The respondent No.1 [NHAI] had preferred the said petition under Section 34(2) of the A & C Act,
impugning NC: 2025:KHC:30771-DB HC-KAR an Arbitral Award dated 26.06.2023 passed by the learned Arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The NHAI is essentially aggrieved by the impugned award as it has enhanced the compensation awarded to respondent No.1 [appellant] for acquisition of his land measuring 3228 square feet located in Survey No. 40/5 of Meena Kunte Village.
It is NHAI's case that the award was unreasonable as it found favour with the learned Commercial Court.

The Arbitrator had enhanced the compensation by adding 75% [50% +
25%] of the gazetted value.
However, it provided no reasons for such enhancement.
The learned Commercial Court also found that the extant instructions for such an enhancement is not applicable.
The appellant being aggrieved by the said decision has filed the present appeal.

sentences.text: A plain reading of the impugned award indicates that it is an unreasoned award and is thus liable to be set aside for that ground alone.
The Arbitral Tribunal had not provided any reasons for enhancing the compensation by NC: 2025:KHC:30771-DB HC-KAR 75%.
In the event NHAI seeks enhanced compensation is required to be agitated, the same may be agitated in Arbitration.
4. We accordingly, dismiss the present appeal.

However, it is clarified that if the appellant seeks a fresh reference within a period of two weeks from today, the time period from the date of the impugned award shall not be considered as a delay on the part of the appellant.
5. We also clarify all other rights and contentions of the parties are reserved, including the NHAI's contention that the initial reference was delayed.
6. Pending IAs, if any, stand disposed of.
